g.text: Learn the parts of a flower by matching the labels to the correct target areas
Click "Hint" for a clue or "Check Answer" to reveal the correct labels.

div.style: font-family: 'Segoe UI', sans-serif; font-size: 14px; color: #475569; line-height: 1.8; text-align: justify;

ul.li: Find the numbered target areas around the flower.
Match the labels in the Word Bank to the correct slot.
Click "Hint" for a helpful clue if you're stuck.
Click "Check Answer" to see the correct labels.

g.text: Pollen lands on the sticky stigma and
grows a tube down the style to reach
Drag & drop these labels onto the correct slots!
The colorful, leaf-like structures that attract pollinators.
The small, green, leaf-like parts that protect the flower bud.
The male reproductive organ of the flower.
The female reproductive organ, located in the center.
The top part of the stamen that produces and releases pollen.
The long, slender stalk that holds up the anther.
The enlarged base of the pistil that contains the ovules.
The narrow neck of the pistil connecting the stigma to the ovary.
The sticky tip of the pistil that captures pollen grains.
The thickened part of the stem where all the flower parts attach.
Check your answers below. Click "Reveal on Diagram" to see the labels mapped directly.
This will highlight the correct labels directly on the flower diagram.
